qa.question: Is Southwest Power Pool entry ERAS-2025-003 at Redbud a new unit or the turbine upgrade?
qa.finding: The Southwest Power Pool entry ERAS-2025-003 lists a 186 MW combined cycle addition at the Redbud 345 kV substation, with commercial operation in January 2027. A state air permit memorandum (https://applications.deq.ok.gov/permitspublic/storedpermits/9021.pdf) says the four existing combustion turbines are being upgraded, which raises the plant from about 1,268 MW to 1,490 MW. The 2026 OG&E resource plan (https://ogeenergy.gcs-web.com/static-files/80b39a4f-b2b2-45cc-b848-efc9ba018dd8) lists no new unit at Redbud.
qa.recommendation: Do not add a new unit. Treat the entry as the capacity increase of the four existing units, and consider raising each unit from 358 MW to about 372.5 MW once the upgrade is confirmed complete.
qa.note: I read the OG&E 2026 resource plan. Its list of planned additions names only Horseshoe Lake and Tinker, and its footnote says OG&E owns 51 percent of Redbud, which matches the shares in the database. I read the queue entry in the Southwest Power Pool open list on 5 November 2026 (https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GenerateActiveCSV). It names OG&E as the owner and gives no turbine count. The EIA-860M table for September 2026 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx) shows no planned generator at this plant. I did not find the other owners' shares in a document beyond the database values, so those stay as they are.

qa.question: Should each Redbud unit's capacity move from 358 MW to 372.5 MW after the upgrade?
qa.finding: The permit memorandum (https://applications.deq.ok.gov/permitspublic/storedpermits/9021.pdf) says each combined cycle unit goes from 317 MW to 372.5 MW. The EIA-860M table for September 2026 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx) still shows 198.9 MW plus 159.5 MW, or 358.4 MW, per unit.
qa.recommendation: Leave 358 MW for now. Change all four units to 372.5 MW when EIA or the owner confirms the upgrade is finished.
qa.note: The memorandum describes planned work, so it does not prove the upgrade is done.
